title: Financial Ledger Aggregation Bug Hunt
scenario: An internal C data pipeline reads raw transaction records from a SQLite database, applies a configurable aggregation engine, and writes daily rollup summaries back to a second SQLite table. The system has ~1200 lines across five C source files plus a runtime config file. An analyst noticed that per-category daily totals started disagreeing with the raw sums about three weeks ago, right after a 'harmless refactoring' was merged. The symptom looks like a rounding bug in the display formatter, but the real breakage is deeper.
instruction_draft: Hey, something's wrong with the ledger pipeline in /app. I've been checking my daily category totals and they don't match the raw transactions in the database — the aggregated numbers are off. The pipeline reads from `ledger.db` (table `raw_txns`) and writes to `ledger.db` (table `daily_rollups`). Running `make && ./ledger_pipeline` should recompute everything. What I need: (1) each row in `daily_rollups` must have a `total_cents` equal to the exact integer sum of `amount_cents` for all raw_txns with matching `category` and `txn_date`; (2) each row's `tx_count` must equal the count of those matching raw transactions; (3) the `category` and `txn_date` values in `daily_rollups` must exactly match what's in the raw data — no dropped categories, no merged dates. Fix the pipeline code so this holds for any data loaded into `raw_txns`.
requirements: Each row in daily_rollups.total_cents equals the exact integer sum of raw_txns.amount_cents grouped by category and txn_date
Each row in daily_rollups.tx_count equals the count of matching raw_txns rows for that category and txn_date
Every (category, txn_date) pair present in raw_txns has a corresponding row in daily_rollups
No (category, txn_date) pair appears in daily_rollups that has no corresponding raw_txns rows
The pipeline must produce correct results for any valid data loaded into raw_txns, not just the pre-seeded sample
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm installs gcc, make, libsqlite3-dev, sqlite3, python3
Five C source files: main.c (~150 lines), db_reader.c (~200 lines), aggregator.c (~300 lines), formatter.c (~180 lines), db_writer.c (~200 lines), plus shared headers
A Makefile that builds the ledger_pipeline binary
A runtime config file /app/pipeline.conf with key=value pairs controlling behavior: AGGREGATION_BUCKET_SIZE, CATEGORY_HASH_SLOTS, DATE_GROUPING_MODE, OVERFLOW_STRATEGY
ledger.db pre-seeded with ~500 raw_txns rows across ~8 categories and ~30 dates, and a partially-correct daily_rollups table

Bug 1 (misleading symptom): formatter.c has an off-by-one in its display-only cents-to-dollars conversion that prints wrong values to stdout — this looks like the source of the mismatch but only affects display output, not the database writes

Bug 2 (real bug A): aggregator.c uses CATEGORY_HASH_SLOTS from pipeline.conf as the size of a fixed hash table for bucketing categories; the config value is set to 7 (a prime), but the hash function uses modulo against a hardcoded 8 (power of two leftover from pre-refactor), causing two categories to collide and their totals to be merged into one bucket, silently dropping one category's output and corrupting another's total

Bug 3 (real bug B): db_writer.c reads DATE_GROUPING_MODE from pipeline.conf; after the refactor the config key was renamed from DATE_GROUP_MODE to DATE_GROUPING_MODE but db_writer.c still reads the old key name, gets NULL, falls back to a default mode that truncates txn_date strings to YYYY-MM (dropping the day), causing all transactions in the same month to be merged into a single date bucket instead of per-day buckets

The two real bugs interact: fixing only the hash collision still produces wrong date grouping; fixing only the date grouping still produces wrong category totals; both must be fixed for cross-component consistency
A Python test harness /app/tests/verify.py that clears raw_txns, loads freshly generated transactions, runs the pipeline, and checks all three requirements against a reference computation
The pre-seeded sample data happens to have only one transaction per month per category in some categories, masking the date-grouping bug on casual inspection
internal_hint: The solver must: (1) notice the formatter stdout discrepancy and investigate whether it affects the DB (it doesn't — red herring); (2) query daily_rollups vs raw_txns directly in sqlite3 to see actual numeric mismatches in the DB; (3) trace through aggregator.c and spot the hardcoded '% 8' vs the config CATEGORY_HASH_SLOTS=7, fix it to use the config value; (4) trace through db_writer.c and notice it calls config_get('DATE_GROUP_MODE') while pipeline.conf has DATE_GROUPING_MODE, fix the key name; (5) recompile and verify. The config file is the cross-component glue — it mediates between components that must agree on key names and on using the config value rather than hardcoded constants.
trap: An agent that fixes only the formatter (the obvious symptom) sees the stdout output look correct on the pre-seeded sample and stops. An agent that finds and fixes only the hash collision bug passes roughly half the generated test cases (those with few categories or single-transaction months). Only fixing both bugs in aggregator.c and db_writer.c produces correct results across all freshly generated inputs, which include months with multiple dates and category counts that stress both hash slots and date grouping.
tests: Test 1 (basic correctness): Load 200 transactions across 6 categories and 10 distinct dates; run pipeline; for each (category, txn_date) pair assert daily_rollups.total_cents == SUM(amount_cents) and tx_count == COUNT(*) from raw_txns

Test 2 (hash slot stress): Load transactions designed so that with slots=7 and modulo-8 hashing, exactly two category names collide; verify both categories appear as separate rows in daily_rollups with correct independent totals

Test 3 (multi-date-per-month stress): Load transactions where the same category appears on 3 different days within the same calendar month; verify 3 separate daily_rollup rows exist for that category, not 1 merged row
Test 4 (zero-count guard): Verify no (category, txn_date) row appears in daily_rollups that has no corresponding raw_txns rows after a fresh load

Test 5 (coverage): Load transactions across all 8 categories used by the seeder, with at least 2 distinct dates per category; verify row count in daily_rollups equals the count of distinct (category, txn_date) pairs in raw_txns

Test 6 (large fuzz): Generate 2000 transactions with random amounts (1..9999999 cents), 12 categories, 60 dates across 3 months; run pipeline; compare every aggregated value against a Python reference computation using integer arithmetic

verifier_knob.name: num_generated_inputs
verifier_knob.effect: Lowering to 100 transactions / 4 categories / 5 dates reduces collision and date-grouping stress, making a partial fix appear to pass; raising to 5000 transactions / 20 categories / 90 dates increases the probability that both bugs manifest and interact in the same test run

expected_failure_modes: Agent fixes only the formatter display bug (the misleading symptom) and verifies against the pre-seeded sample, which looks correct in stdout
Agent finds the hash collision bug and fixes it but never investigates the date-grouping config key mismatch, passing tests with few dates per month but failing multi-date tests
Agent fixes the config key name mismatch but not the hardcoded modulo constant, passing date tests but failing category collision tests
Agent rewrites aggregation logic from scratch in a way that works for the sample but introduces an off-by-one or integer overflow for large generated amounts

Agent patches the config parsing to be case-insensitive or fuzzy-matching (masking the key name bug) but the hardcoded modulo remains, causing intermittent failures depending on generated category names
